talks.title: John Strand - A Quick, Efficient Yet Not Entirely Sane Introduction to Deception (BSidesFrankfurt 20
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of John Strand - A Quick, Efficient Yet Not Entirely Sane Introduction to Deception (BSidesFrankfurt 20.
talks.summary:
Overview: John Strand presents at BSides Frankfurt on deception technology, offering a practical yet unconventional introduction to active defense using MITRE's SHIELD Engage framework.

Key Topics: Why deception matters when perimeter detection fails; common mistakes in threat intelligence feed consumption; the SHIELD Engage framework for deception operations; and building detection that doesn't depend on vendor promises alone.

Technical Details: Strand critiques over-reliance on SIEM and SOAR solutions, arguing defenders need internal visibility through deception. He covers honeypots, honeytokens, and adversary engagement techniques mapped to MITRE SHIELD tactics.

Takeaways: Deception provides high-fidelity detection when traditional perimeter tools miss intruders. Effective programs require understanding attacker behavior and integrating deception into broader detection strategies.

talks.title: Waseem Ajrab & Julian Petersohn
talks.teaser: Identify examines Waseem Ajrab & Julian Petersohn.
talks.summary:
SAP Attack Surface

Wasim Ajrab and Julian Petersohn map SAP’s scale—hundreds of millions of lines of code, sprawling ERP processes, routers, gateways, and cloud connectors. Legacy RFC/DI protocols from the 1990s lacked encryption by default, exposing business, healthcare, and financial data paths.

Cloud and AI Expansion

SAP pushes RISE managed offerings and Joule AI while customers receive lengthy add-on security service lists. Presenters argue complexity and proprietary stacks multiply patch and monitoring burden; AI features have already introduced vulnerabilities in customer cloud environments.

Common Security Myths

They debunk beliefs that SAP is “secure by default” because it is German-made, that zero trust is a purchasable SAP product, and that identity management alone secures the platform. SAP Basis teams often lack hardening skills; controls concentrate on production while dev/staging networks stay flat and interconnected across hyperscalers.

Red Team Perspective

Standard passwords and overlooked interfaces beyond IAM illustrate why SAP complexity aids attackers. The talk urges holistic network segmentation and specialist defense rather than isolating authorization teams with large budgets but narrow scope.

talks.title: Alexander Andersson - Demystifying Cloud Infrastructure Attacks (BSidesFrankfurt 2024)
talks.teaser: Industry experts analyze emerging threats surrounding Alexander Andersson - Demystifying Cloud Infrastructure Attacks (BSidesFrankfurt 2024).
talks.summary:
Cloud Kill Chains

Truesec forensic consultant Alexander Andersson asks what classic on-prem DMZ-to-domain-admin attacks look like in cloud environments, using composite real incident screenshots.

Password Reset Timeline Matters

A case that looked benign after MFA enforcement and PC rebuild changed when timestamps showed password reset, device enrollment, then single-factor login—likely attacker persistence via self-service recovery methods.

Hybrid Identity Models

He explains federation with ADFS token signing, pass-through authentication queues on AD Connect, and password hash sync with MD4-derived cloud hashes. Each hybrid mode enables distinct attacker paths if on-prem components are compromised.

Forensic Lessons

Investigators must trace sync accounts, security info updates, and hybrid-specific persistence instead of closing cases after credential rotation alone.

talks.title: Milenko Starcik - Cybersecurity for Space Systems (BSidesFrankfurt 2024)
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Milenko Starcik - Cybersecurity for Space Systems (BSidesFrankfurt 2024).
talks.summary:
Core message

Milenko Starcik (Vision Space Systems) argues space cybersecurity mirrors OT/industrial challenges—expensive, long-lived systems with outsized impact when weather, imaging, telecom, or GNSS/PNT services fail.

Architecture

Space ecosystems span ground segment (control/payload ops, launch), spacecraft (single science platforms to mega-constellations), and user segment (phones, emergency messaging, emerging 5G NTN).

Threat landscape

Beyond flashy kinetic attacks (ASAT, lasers, docking/dragging satellites), electromagnetic threats include GPS jamming/spoofing and RF link attacks; cyber adds familiar IT-style risks with harder attribution.

Actor model

Sophisticated threats are often nation-state driven; kinetic actions are visible, while cyber offers plausible deniability—policy treats non-physical attacks as lower escalation, encouraging probing (e.g., Baltic GPS interference).

Takeaway

Space security is not rocket-science exceptionalism—the same distributed, privileged, long-lived system problems apply at global scale.

talks.title: Aaron Jewitt - Zero Trust
talks.teaser: Attack analyzes Aaron Jewitt - Zero Trust.
talks.summary:
## Zero Trust Beyond Marketing

Aaron Jewitt of Elastic addresses BSides Frankfurt on zero trust from offensive and defensive angles. Definitions vary by vendor, but the core principle—never trust, always verify—collides with reality when organizations deploy dozens of privileged agents on every endpoint.

## The Agent Sprawl Problem

EDR, vulnerability scanners, asset managers, and remote-support tools each install kernel-level or high-privilege agents. Attackers target the management plane; defenders struggle to inventory trusted code they never authorized. Jewitt compares zero trust to a cult where endpoints trust only the EDR—until a bad update, echoing CrowdStrike's global outage, proves blind trust fails.

## Attacking Identity Perimeters

Red-team techniques include Evilginx-style adversary-in-the-middle proxies that harvest credentials and session tokens despite TLS padlocks. Passkeys with certificate pinning and device-bound authentication resist these attacks; pairing WebAuthn with device attestation through Okta Verify or Windows Hello raises the bar further.

## Detection and Prevention Together

Jewitt emphasizes no prevention is perfect. Blue teams need telemetry on anomalous agent behavior, impossible-travel logins, and token replay alongside architectural controls. Zero trust succeeds when identity, device health, and continuous verification align—not when a single product checkbox claims the architecture complete.
